title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 20–27. The patching priority is php2shell: CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct. 26, and the catalog due date is Oct. 29. The VeloCloud and Collabora entries, both due Oct. 26, were dropped because they are no longer the current priority. CISA also published the CISA 2030 strategy on Oct. 26. No CISA alert dated Oct. 27 was found. Federal News Network's Oct. 26 account of the CMMC request for information is included. No new public update on the DMDC personnel breach was found.

items.headline: CISA puts php2shell on the KEV list, with a catalog due date of Oct. 29
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-109618, a PHP memory-corruption bug, and CVE-2026-109619, a stale internal request-state bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct. 26. The catalog sets a due date of Oct. 29 for both. CISA's php2shell alert, revised the same day, says the bugs allow unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP that serves web requests, names Apache with mod_php as the configuration PHP considers highest risk, and says to update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. CISA says organizations that cannot update immediately, or that still run PHP 8.1 or earlier, should take those systems offline until they are patched.

items.headline: Microsoft says Storm-0940 used an AI pentest framework in the ConnectWise compromise
items.summary: Microsoft said Oct. 21 that Storm-0940, which it describes as a China-state-aligned actor, used the open-source agentic penetration-testing framework ARTEX and was responsible for the ConnectWise multi-tenant application compromise. After that access, Microsoft said, the actor used ARTEX to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants at 2,900 attempts per minute, and in multiple cases reached privileged cloud access in under three hours. Microsoft said the activity did not come from a flaw in Microsoft's own products, and that an affected application or a successful sign-in does not by itself mean customer data was taken. Its guidance is to keep the affected ConnectWise application connections disabled until ConnectWise publishes restoration instructions, and to review activity from at least Oct. 15.

items.headline: CISA publishes a 2030 strategy with 60-, 180- and 365-day milestones
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 26 it released CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail. Acting Director Nick Andersen called on critical-infrastructure owners, operators, vendors and technology manufacturers to act, and the release says the strategy is meant to identify, disrupt and eliminate adversarial access. CISA names three pillars: Defend, lead national cyber defense; Harden, prioritize national infrastructure security; and Prevail, mobilize national resilience. The release says CISA will begin reviewing core services within 60 days, provide an implementation plan within 180 days, and report progress within 365 days. It also says CISA will keep its role, delegated by Homeland Security, in starting and restoring National Security and Emergency Preparedness communications.

items.headline: Federal News Network: CMMC cost complaints in the RFI point at NIST 800-171, not the assessments
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Oct. 26 that the Defense Department reviewed 997 responses to its Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification request for information, 509 of them (51 percent) from the defense industrial base, and that an internal email lists NIST Special Publication 800-171 work, including Microsoft 365 GCC High, enclaves and inconsistent interpretation, as the top cost concern rather than CMMC itself. The outlet says the RFI put the average cost of CMMC, separate from NIST 800-171, at $47,000, and it quotes the department on that same average assessment cost, set against Kelly Loeffler's July statement that complying could cost as much as $600,000. Federal News Network says the review is past the 75 days Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies set in July, that the department declined to comment, and that as of September 2,433 companies had Level 2 third-party certifications.

items.headline: SafePay advisory: about 600 victims, initial access through edge devices and stolen passwords
items.summary: CISA, the FBI, the Secret Service and international partners released a StopRansomware advisory on SafePay dated Oct. 20. A CISA news release the next day says the group has hit about 600 victims across the Americas, Europe and Australia and is one of the most active ransomware groups of 2026. Actors steal or guess passwords, use phishing, and exploit known vulnerabilities on internet-facing devices, often arriving through VPN, then create or take over accounts, move with legitimate admin tools, disable backups, steal data and encrypt systems. Listed bugs include CVE-2020-3259, CVE-2023-20269, CVE-2023-27532, CVE-2024-40711 and CVE-2024-40766, and CISA's ask is to patch edge devices, require multifactor authentication, restrict admin tools, segment networks and keep offline backups that have been restored in a test.

items.headline: Cisco: eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys can be brute-forced, and firewalls are still under review
items.summary: Cisco's informational advisory, first published Oct. 23 and updated Oct. 24, says a researcher showed that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates can be brute-forced in seconds because of an error in an April 2025 key ceremony, and that anyone with those keys can issue fraudulent TLS certificates for any domain. Cisco says two of the eight are code-signing CAs, and that all eight were cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025. Cisco PSIRT said it is not aware of malicious use. Secure Firewall Management Center has a remediation article, while Secure Firewall ASA, Threat Defense, and Identity Services Engine were still under investigation in the Oct. 24 update.
